correctness.rationale: The determinant-one normalization sends an integer-area core to an index-q integer sublattice. Rational rank two then gives the same irrational/rational rogue normal form. The Zak return is Laurent because the core vectors remain integral. The new finite-index lemma follows from a degree-q torus covering and the at-most-two-zero target trinomial. Inspection of the source proof after its finite-zero step shows that all later lemmas use only the resulting finite exceptional set, irrational return, zero-free active arc, and Laurent structure. These hypotheses are preserved.

value.rationale: Positive integer area is a structurally natural infinite slice of the supercritical mixed-arithmetic frontier: exactly there the marked core normalizes to a finite-index sublattice of the Zak lattice. The theorem extends all-L2 independence from the critical q=1 boundary to every q>=2 and identifies a reusable mechanism—finite coverings preserve the finite-zero property needed by the holonomy proof. This is a substantive classification extension, not an arbitrary parameter substitution.
